To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have proposed a game theoretic approach to obtain an optimal control strategy for a cyber-physical system in the presence of a replay attack, and have shown the existence of a solution to the game and have proposed an algorithm that calculates a suboptimal solution to the game.

(1) we propose a game theoretic approach to minimize the cost of replay attacks in a control system, (2) we formulate a stochastic game model that incorporates the system's dynamics, the control system, the replay detector, and the attacker's behavior, (3) we prove that the proposed model is a finite-horizon stationary stochastic game, and we present a suboptimum algorithm to compute the optimal control strategy for the system, (4) we present a simulation example that demonstrates

a) a game-theoretic approach can be used to find a trade-off between the security overhead of a system and its performance in the presence of replay attacks, and b) the optimal strategy exists and can be found using a suboptimal solution to a stationary stochastic game.
